text:
zoe: quick heads-up — support pinged about customers seeing "validation error" billing hits when tools return slightly malformed JSON (e.g. array at top level).

nav: example please?

zoe: minimal: ```json
[{"name":"status","code":0}]
```

zoe: our schema expects an object `{name: string, code: integer}` so validator treats as "fncall.validation_failure" and today increments invoke.quota_rejects which customers interpret as a charged failed call.

harry: hmm that's been longstanding. We collapsed soft vs hard into one metric to avoid lots of billing rule branches. Bad UX though.

maya: proposal: decouple billing from soft failures. New metric set: invoke.validator.hard and invoke.validator.soft. Only hard maps to quota/billing. Soft shows in console as "Validation warning" (yellow) and not charged.

nav: agree, but need to be careful about routing: some codepaths currently detect validator failures and route to degen-model to avoid charges. We must not change routing behavior unintentionally. Soft -> keep existing fallback route. Only billing tag changes.

zoe: telemetry changes: add tag validator.error_kind with values [top_level_array, missing_required, bad_type, parse_fail, unknown_field]. Also include route_name and model_snapshot for correlation. Sampling: keep full payloads for 100% hard, 0.5% soft, and add a separate retention TTL for sampled soft payloads (7d).

harry: also add metric validator.coercion_used (bool) and a counter for coercion_fallbacks so we can tune heuristics.

maya: console: split Errors into two tabs: Errors (red) and Warnings (yellow). Warnings should show sample count, common patterns (e.g. top_level_array: 42%), and a single-click "Create schema exception" action which persists an allowlist for that tool signature.

nav: rollout: feature flag fncall.soft_billing_exempt. Start internal only, then 5% customer canary for 1 week, then 25% for another week, then GA. Must coordinate with billing team — they'll need to ensure historic invoices don't change.

zoe: API surface: introduce invocation_options.validator_mode with values [legacy, permissive, strict]. Default legacy keeps current behavior for now. SDKs can set permissive to opt out of strict billing or strict to force hard reject.

harry: alerts: create alert if any route's hard_reject_rate > 0.02% over 10m. Soft spike alert but lower severity at 1% over 10m. Also alert if coercion_used ratio > 5% on any route.

maya: implementation notes: validator should return a normalized result to router: `{"outcome":"soft","why":"top_level_array","coerced":true,"fallback_route":"fallback-v2","sample_id":"s-xyz"}`. Router uses outcome for monitoring only. Billing system reads the billing_tag field which will be set to billed/unbilled per new mapping.

nav: storage/PII concern: sampled payloads may contain user PII. Add scrubber stage before storing and include a config toggle to disable payload sampling per-account.

zoe: short mitigation: flip feature flag that stops mapping soft -> quota in our billing pipeline immediately for internal orgs. If green, widen to canary.

harry: will open PR to add metrics + tags and the new validator result contract.
maya: I'll mock console UI and the "Create schema exception" flow. nav: I'll coordinate with billing and infra to plan canary and sampling scrubbing.

infra-bot: ACTIONS_CREATED: INV-12211 (validator-metrics), UI-7802 (console-warnings-tab), SAMP-9901 (soft-sample-pipeline), CANARY-2026-04-07 scheduled. Owners: harry, maya, nav. ETA: prototypes in 4 business days.

zoe: thanks folks — let's jugaad this carefully; customers are confused and we should avoid surprise invoice changes. Will follow up in next sync. :thumbsup:
